# 02 audit -- geo_index_core code (contrib/geo_index_core/)

## Round 1 -- 2026-11-19T14:30Z

- Scope: the whole new directory `contrib/geo_index_core/` (uncommitted at audit time): `include/geo_index/{cell,cover}.h`,
  `src/{cell,cover}.cpp`, `src/check.h`, `test/{cell,cover}_test.cpp`, `test/data/gen_fixtures.py` + fixtures,
  `CMakeLists.txt`, `run_tests.sh`, `Dockerfile`.  State audited: 8/8 tests green under ASan+UBSan, valgrind 0 errors.
- Agent / model: `code-review` / `gpt-6-astra` (author: claude).  Per R-AUDIT.
- Result: 4 findings (3 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM), 4 fixed, 0 rejected.  All three HIGH findings were real bugs the
  green test run did not catch.

### 1. HIGH -- `cover()` misses points on a covering cell's boundary (`src/cover.cpp:38-48`)
- Evidence (auditor reproduced on S2 0.10.0): region = `S2Cell(face 1)`, which contains (lat 0, lon 45).
  `cover(region, 0, 8)` = `[-5764607523034234880, -5764607523034234880]`, but `cell_of(0, 45, 0)` =
  `-8070450532247928832`, which is outside that range.  The same miss happens at levels 1, 10 and 30.
  Cause: an `S2Cell` is closed, but `S2CellId(point)` assigns a boundary point to only ONE of the
  adjacent cells.
- Why the tests missed it: every fixture region was a polygon, and no fixture point sat exactly on an
  S2 cell edge.
- Fix: the API is narrowed to `cover(const S2Polygon&, ...)`.  The covering is grown by a radius > 0
  (`S2CellUnion::Expand(S1Angle::Radians(1e-9), 3)`), so every point of the old union lies strictly inside
  the new one.  Expand also re-normalizes the union, which the range merge needs.  Cost: at most
  4*(1+2^3) = 36x cells before merging, with a buffer of about 1/8 of the largest cell
  (`# kiss:` ceiling noted in the code; revisit at Z.3 if the buffer costs more than 1% of rows).
  Regression test `GeoIndexCover.PointOnCoveringCellEdgeIsCovered` uses the face-1 square as a
  polygon and the auditor's (0, 45) point, at levels 0/1/10/30.

### 2. HIGH -- the core library was not sanitizer-instrumented (`CMakeLists.txt:29,41-43`)
- Evidence: `add_library(geo_index_core)` ran before `add_compile_options(-fsanitize=...)`.  CMake copies the
  directory options into a target when the target is created, so `cell.cpp` and `cover.cpp` were built
  without ASan or UBSan.  Only the test files were instrumented.  The earlier "ASan clean" result
  therefore did not cover the library code.
- Fix: the sanitizer options are now set before any target is created; the library target is defined once,
  after them, for both the standalone and the in-Doris build.

### 3. HIGH -- `-U__SANITIZE_ADDRESS__` workaround is GCC-only (`CMakeLists.txt:37-42`)
- Background: the system `libs2`/absl are built without ASan.  When absl detects ASan it adds generation
  fields to its btree nodes, so our inline absl code and the prebuilt `libs2` disagree on the layout.  The
  first test run showed this as a false "invalidated iterator" abort.  Undefining `__SANITIZE_ADDRESS__`
  fixed that under GCC.
- Evidence: under Clang, absl also detects ASan through `__has_feature(address_sanitizer)`, which cannot
  be turned off.  The auditor reproduced the layout mismatch: the fixture test hung.
- Fix: the workaround is now used only with GCC (ASan + UBSan).  With Clang (macOS) the build is UBSan
  only and prints a CMake STATUS line saying so.  ASan and valgrind run in the Linux Docker reference
  environment.

### 4. MEDIUM -- macOS run forced LeakSanitizer (`run_tests.sh:38`)
- Evidence: Apple Clang's ASan runtime has no LeakSanitizer, so `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1` aborts every
  test there.
- Fix: `detect_leaks` is set to 0 on Darwin.  This option is moot now that Clang builds are UBSan only
  (finding 3), but it stays correct if ASan is added back.

### Verification after the fixes (2026-11-19T14:40Z)
- `run_tests.sh` in Docker: "100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 9" (GCC ASan+UBSan), valgrind
  "ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors", "All heap blocks were freed", "== all clean".
- Finding 2 verified: `nm libgeo_index_core.a | grep -c __asan_` = 35; before the fix the library had no ASan symbols.
- Finding 1 NOT verified by the regression test.  A probe (`/tmp/probe`, not checked in) checked 19,548 points
  lying exactly on S2 cell vertices / edge midpoints of covering cells, inside 300 random polygons, at
  levels 8/12/16: 0 misses WITH Expand and 0 misses WITHOUT it.  `PointOnCoveringCellEdgeIsCovered` also
  passes with Expand reverted.  So for `S2Polygon` input (the narrowed API) the boundary miss has not
  been reproduced.  The auditor's repro used a bare `S2Cell` region, which the API no longer accepts.
  Why it is likely safe without Expand: if the polygon has area on the neighbour cell's side of the
  point, the neighbour intersects the polygon, so the covering must include it.  The only remaining
  case is a point exactly on the polygon boundary, and Doris' `ST_Contains` already excludes points
  on edges (02.audit.design.md #3), so a miss there cannot change a query result.
- Decision: Expand stays for now (cheap to remove, and it errs toward correctness).  Plan 02 A.4 adds a
  checked-in property test that would catch a real miss.  Plan 02 P.1 measures Expand's cost (ranges,
  candidate rows) and removes it if the property test passes without it (R-KISS).
- Re-audit: round 2 (`gpt-6-astra`, fix diff + A.4) to be appended here.
